## High Level Overview of Change

Spec: [XLS-46d: Dynamic Non Fungible Tokens (dNFTs)](https://github.com/XRPLF/XRPL-Standards/discussions/130)

This Amendment adds functionality to update the URI of [NFToken objects](https://github.com/XRPLF/XRPL-Standards/discussions/46) by adding:

`NFTokenModify:` Transactor to initiate the altering of the URI
`lsfMutable`: Flag to be set in a NFTokenMint transaction to allow NFTokenModify to execute successfully on given NFT.

Nice job on this pull request!  The unit test coverage is pretty good.  I appreciate that you took the time to do that.

I left quite a number of comments, but don't be dismayed by that ...

That said, I think that my comment regarding the `nft::updateToken()` implementation is pretty important.  If you choose not to implement that change I'll want to understand why.

For your convenience I made commits that implement all of the changes I've suggested.  If you want, you're welcome to cherry pick them, or you can just use them as examples of the changes I am suggesting.  The

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body: The spec (https://github.com/XRPLF/XRPL-Standards/discussions/130 August 18, 2023 version) specifies that the `sfURI` field is required.  Here it is listed as `soeOPTIONAL`. I think that `soeOPTIONAL` is a good choice, because that matches the behavior of `NFTokenMint`.  Perhaps the spec needs to be updated?

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body: I think "minter" is not a great name for the role this `Account` plays in this test.  They certainly do mint the NFTs, but not in the role assigned by `setMinter()`.  I think a better name for this `Account` would be "issuer".  Issuer really is the role that this `Account` plays throughout the unit test.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body:
It looks like this section of the test is exercising corners of `NFTokenModify::preflight()`.  That's great, and I very much appreciate it.

There is a corner of `preflight()` that this test currently misses.  You can verify that `preflight()` calls `preflight1()` by causing a `preflight1()` to return a non-`tesSUCCESS` code.  Here's one way to do that:
```
            // Set a negative fee.  Exercises invalid preflight1.
            env(token::modify(issuer, nftId),
                fee(STAmount(10ull, true)),
                ter(temBAD_FEE));
```

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
```
reviewCommentsList.body:
My personal bias is to use real type names, rather than `auto` as long at the type name does not get too long.  I find this really helps me when I'm reading code.  I use a text editor, not an IDE, to work on code.  So having the actual type be visible in the source code makes it easier for me as a reader.

If you use an IDE you might think this guidance does not apply to you.  But if you use the Github interface to do code reviews, then you too read code as text.  So having the actual type visible in the source code benefits you as well.

That's a long winded way of suggesting that you replace the `auto` with `TER`.  But I'm not insisting.  It's only a suggestion.
```

I think there's a problem with the `nft::updateToken()` implementation.  See the discussion in `NFTokenUtils.cpp`.  I'm going to suggest that all of this code be replaced by...
```
    return nft::changeTokenURI(view(), owner, nftokenID, ctx_.tx[~sfURI]);
```

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body:
This implementation for `updateToken` has a subtle complexity hidden in it.  The current behavior is to remove the `NFToken` from the page and then insert the `NFToken` into the (presumably same) page.

The subtle complexity is that removing the `NFToken` from its page may cause the page to coalesce with adjacent pages.  Then re-adding the `NFToken` may cause the page to split.  None of that activity is really necessary.  We're not actually removing or adding an `NFToken`.  We're just adding, replacing or removing the `URI` associated with the `NFToken`.  The presence of the `NFToken`, and its `NFTokenID` value, are always left unchanged.  So manipulating NFTokenPages is not really necessary

reviewCommentsList.body: Is there any use case for removing the URI from an existing NFT? Is there any difference from burning the NFT compared to an NFT without a URI?

reviewCommentsList.author: tequdev
reviewCommentsList.body:
Such a use case may not be common, but it is not impossible to say that there is no use case.

Since the NFTokenMint transaction can be executed with the URI field unspecified, it is reasonable that the NFTokenModify transaction can change the URI field to unspecified.
